local-ollama.json.name: local-ollama

Swap the model names for whatever you've pulled (`ollama pull <model>`); swap `baseUrl` if Ollama (or an LM Studio / other OpenAI-compatible local runner) listens somewhere other than the default `http://localhost:11434/v1`.
local-ollama.json.summary: Every seat on a local Ollama model: no API key and no spend.

mock-budget.json.name: mock-budget
mock-budget.json.description: Offline, and the only mock chain that costs anything on paper. Its seats use mock/mock-priced, a $1000-per-Mtok test fixture price, so the per-run spend cap can be exercised without a key or a real call: run it with --max-usd 1 to watch a run stop cleanly, then resume it with a higher ceiling.

mock-criteria-kinds.json.name: mock-criteria-kinds
mock-criteria-kinds.json.description: Offline. Calls no API and costs nothing. The mock chain with criterion kinds on: every criterion is checkable (with its command) or judgement, and the board counts them.

mock-debate.json.name: mock-debate
mock-debate.json.description: Offline. Proposal stage plus the debate and reply rounds (anonymised), the board handed to the builder, withdrawn/amended proposals, a handoff file at the end.

mock-dispute.json.name: mock-dispute
mock-dispute.json.description: Offline. Exercises the dispute stage and its stall rule: one holdout critic raises the same objection every round, so the run stops early instead of burning the full round cap on an argument that is not moving, records the unresolved dissent at the top of the deliverable, and still reports no consensus. The round cap is deliberately high (7) so a test can prove the stall rule stopped the run rather than the cap doing it.

mock-external.json.name: mock-external
mock-external.json.description: Offline. The builder and reviser are external seats: the run pauses, writes NEEDS-<label>.md, and resumes from disk after <label>.md is written. Every other stage is mock.

mock-layered.json.name: mock-layered
mock-layered.json.description: Offline. Exercises the layered review panel (seats.critics[].layer): layer 1 reviews first, layer 2 is asked only when layer 1 signed off, layer 3 only when layer 2 did. The default mock critics fail an unrevised draft and pass the revised one, so round 1 stops at layer 1 (layers 2 and 3 are recorded as not asked), the reviser fixes the draft, and round 2 climbs through all three layers and signs off. The dispute stage is on so a run that does not climb all the way records what is still open.

mock-open.json.name: mock-open
mock-open.json.description: Offline. Proposal stage plus the debate and reply rounds (anonymised), the board handed to the builder, withdrawn/amended proposals, a handoff file at the end.

mock-partitioned.json.name: mock-partitioned
mock-partitioned.json.description: Offline. Exercises v1 context partitioning (config.proposals.partition): one proposer seat (mock-a) gets a per-seat focus instruction, one (mock-b) is deliberately left out of `slices` and gets no instruction, proving partial partitioning and that an unsliced seat's prompt is unaffected. Mechanism only - no claim this changes proposal quality or diversity.

slices.mock-a: Focus on the config schema and validation surface.

mock-patch-fallback.json.name: mock-patch-fallback
mock-patch-fallback.json.description: Offline. Exercises the patch-mode reviser (src/patch-revise.js): a block whose SEARCH text is not in the draft, proving the fallback to one full rewrite.

mock-patch.json.name: mock-patch
mock-patch.json.description: Offline. Exercises the patch-mode reviser (src/patch-revise.js): search/replace blocks applied locally, so text nobody objected to stays byte-identical.

mock-proposals.json.name: mock-proposals
mock-proposals.json.description: Offline. Exercises the proposal stage: skeleton, blind proposals from every critic seat (one of them unreadable), integration with a scope ledger, the scoreboard. Best-of-N: three attempts per lab, a mock judge keeps two.

mock-questions-wait.json.name: mock-questions-wait
mock-questions-wait.json.description: Offline. Questions-first stage that PAUSES for answers (NEEDS-answers.md -> answers.md -> --resume).

mock-questions.json.name: mock-questions
mock-questions.json.description: Offline. Questions-first stage with defaults taken automatically (wait: false), then the debate chain.

mock-relay.json.name: mock-relay
mock-relay.json.description: Offline. Exercises the relay panel branch (each critic is handed the verdicts before it) before spending anything real on it.

mock-security-review.json.name: mock-security-review
mock-security-review.json.description: Offline. Exercises the final security-review gate at $0: a mock build and panel, then the security-review stage last, with a mock reviewer that always reports one high-severity finding - so the gate's blocking path (security-review.json, report.json security_review, CLI exit code 7) runs end to end with no key. Swap seats.security_reviewer's model to mock-security-clean for the passing path.

mock-tiered.json.name: mock-tiered
mock-tiered.json.description: Offline. A tiered council at $0 (tiered councils, 2026-09-26): mass seats (seats.proposers) propose parts, debate them and post on the architectures; anchor seats (seats.alternatives) write the whole architectures and reply; the anchor panel (seats.critics) alone votes. The majority guard is on: authors see arguments without lab letters or counts, and a withdrawal that quotes no argument (mock-yield-unargued, mock-alt-withdraw) stays for the builder while one that does (mock-yield-argued) is honoured. A deep-dive seat reads the task in 1000-character chunks, once per focus entry, under its own cap and maxCalls, and the reviser answers its findings before the panel's first review.

mock-unanimous.json.name: mock-unanimous
mock-unanimous.json.description: Offline. Exercises the unanimous-signoff branch (all critics review every round, not round-robin) before spending anything real on it.

mock.json.name: mock
mock.json.description: Offline. Calls no API and costs nothing. Exercises every branch of the chain so the plumbing can be tested before any key exists.

plan-china-high-council.json.name: plan-china-high-council
plan-china-high-council.json.description: The Chinese High Council (0.8.3): an alternative route next to the three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council), not a replacement for any of them, with the shape of plan-high-council. It runs the planning stages with six proposers (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Tencent HY4 Preview, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiniMax M3), an alternatives stage (GLM-5.3, MiMo V2.6 Pro and Qwen 3.8 Max; every proposer also debates the architectures), one deep-dive seat (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and a layered review panel of twelve named judges in three layers: layer 1 GLM-5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiniMax M3, MiMo V2.6 Pro, Tencent HY4 Preview, StepFun Step 5 Preview; layer 2 DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro; layer 3 GLM-5.3 and Qwen 3.8 Max. Every proposer, alternatives seat, deep-dive seat and judge is a model from a Chinese lab. Tencent HY4 Preview and StepFun Step 5 Preview are preview models. Exactly these twelve judge seats vote; they are filled by nine models from seven companies, and the review panel counts nine labs, one per model, because a model that sits in two layers is one lab, not two. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Tencent HY4 Preview, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiniMax M3 and GLM-5.3 each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain allows 7 such overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds) and, inside one round, 7 revisions of layer 1 and 3 of layer 2 (layerRevisions). When the overseer-round limit or layer 1's revision limit is reached the run stops, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose: continue (it extends the limit that was reached; the run's spending limit still applies), or finish (the dispute stage and the handoff run and the result stays "not agreed"), or revise the draft yourself. When layer 2 has used its revisions in an overseer round and objects again, the plan goes up to layer 3 instead of stopping, while a pass is left. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria stage is answered through your Claude subscription (the Opus 5.5 seat, `provider: external`). The skeleton, build, revise, handoff and decider stages are answered by your Claude Code session (`provider: external`). A stage that waits for an external answer pauses the run with exit code 3 until it is answered. These Claude-backed stages are the only exceptions to the Chinese-model roster. Every API seat reasons at high; no Grok, no Kimi, no Mistral. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 384,000; MiMo V2.6 Pro, GLM-5.3 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max and GLM-5.3 131,072; Tencent HY4 Preview and StepFun Step 5 Preview 64,000. For MiniMax M3 no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Dry run (0.8.3, prices of 2026-11-01, the dry run's assumed sizes): $23.16 expected (every overseer round ends after one climb through the layers) and an upper estimate of $2055.63 (every allowed revision used in every overseer round), about $23.16 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate leaves out the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat), up to 2 consecutive passes that re-ask a silent seat, the explicit asks of a silent judge, answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($2055.63) and the cheapest end ($14.50, one overseer round, the dry run's floor) are above the default cap of $7, the figure the dry run compares a chain with; on the command line your limit is the number you type. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $10 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default this chain probably cannot finish (an inference from the dry run's floor, not a run): raise the ceiling setting first. This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run.
plan-china-high-council.json.summary: Twelve judge seats, six proposers, all Chinese labs; criteria: Opus 5.5 subscription; writer and decider: the session.

Sonnet 5.5 sits in layers 1 and 2 and Opus 5.5 in layers 2 and 3 as separate seats, each answered in its own fresh session, so the two see neither each other's reasoning nor the session that wrote the plan; nothing in the harness checks that the sessions were separate. Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. Every seat is external (provider external): each one pauses the run (exit 3) until it is answered, so a run stops for every proposal, debate post, reply and verdict, up to 24 judge answers at the limits. A Claude Code session can answer the stops one by one with the external_prompt and submit_stage tools, starting a fresh sub-agent on each seat's model for each answer. plan-high-council.json.description: The High Council (0.8.3): the most thorough of three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council), with the strongest models. It runs the planning stages with six proposers (Tencent HY4 Preview, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Muse Spark 1.3, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiMo V2.6 Pro), an alternatives stage (GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3; every proposer also debates the architectures), one deep-dive seat (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and a layered review panel of twelve named judges in three layers: layer 1 GLM-5.3, MiMo V2.6 Pro, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, MiniMax M3, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna; layer 2 Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, Qwen 3.8 Max, Mistral Large 4; layer 3 Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. Exactly these twelve vote, twelve judges from eight companies (Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 are one company, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra are one company); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, MiMo V2.6 Pro, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and GLM-5.3 each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain allows 7 such overseer rounds (maxOverseerRounds) and, inside one round, 7 revisions of layer 1 and 3 of layer 2 (layerRevisions). When the overseer-round limit or layer 1's revision limit is reached the run stops, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose: continue (it extends the limit that was reached; the run's spending limit still applies), or finish (the dispute stage and the handoff run and the result stays "not agreed"), or revise the draft yourself. When layer 2 has used its revisions in an overseer round and objects again, the plan goes up to layer 3 instead of stopping, while a pass is left. Claude Haiku 5.5 (layer 1), Claude Opus 5.5 (layer 2) and Claude Fable 5.1 (layer 3) are answered through your own Claude subscription (provider external, subscription:haiku-5.5, subscription:opus-5.5, subscription:fable-5.1): like the criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages, each pauses the run (exit 3) until it is answered, and the answers should come from a separate fresh session, not the one that wrote the plan. Without a Claude subscription, replace each of those seats with its API seat: {"provider":"openrouter","model":"anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5","maxTokens":128000,"lab":"haiku5.5","extra":{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}},"layer":1}; {"provider":"openrouter","model":"anthropic/claude-opus-5.5","maxTokens":128000,"lab":"opus5.5","extra":{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}},"layer":2}; {"provider":"openrouter","model":"anthropic/claude-fable-5.1","maxTokens":128000,"lab":"fable5.1","extra":{"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}},"layer":3}; the other stages still need a Claude Code session. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages need a Claude Code session (provider external): they pause the run (exit 3) until the session answers. Every API seat reasons at high; no Grok, no Kimi. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; Qwen 3.8 Max, MiMo V2.6 Pro and GLM-5.3 131,072; GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Astra 128,000; Gemini 3.8 Flash 65,536; Tencent HY4 Preview 64,000. For Muse Spark 1.3, MiniMax M3 and Mistral Large 4 no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Dry run (0.8.3, prices of 2026-11-01, the dry run's assumed sizes): $31.57 expected (every overseer round ends after one climb through the layers) and an upper estimate of $2367.57 (every allowed revision used in every overseer round), about $31.57 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate leaves out the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat), up to 2 consecutive passes that re-ask a silent seat, the explicit asks of a silent judge, answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($2367.57) and the cheapest end ($18.44, one overseer round, the dry run's floor) are above the default cap of $7. On the command line that cap is only a suggestion. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $10 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default this chain probably cannot finish (an inference from the dry run's floor, not a run): raise the ceiling setting first. This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run. The review judges' proposals and improvement ideas are quoted; the writer's answers are its own claim, and no judge gives a verdict on them. If the reviser is your Claude Code session, it may propose to finish early. The overseer layer decides whether to say yes. A yes ends the review as not agreed and hands every remaining open objection to the builder as a task.

plan-the-high-council.json.name: plan-the-high-council
plan-the-high-council.json.summary: Twelve judges in three layers and three proposers: four Claude seats on Anthropic, eleven models on OpenRouter.
plan-the-high-council.json.description: The High Council on a new roster (0.8.4, not released yet): a planning chain with three proposers (Claude Sonnet 5.5, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Gemini 4 Argon) and a layered review panel of twelve judges in three layers: layer 1 Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, GLM-5.3 Flash, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; layer 2 Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Terra, MiMo V2.6 Pro, Hy4 Preview, Qwen 3.8 27B; layer 3 Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6.1 Sol. Each of its fifteen proposer and judge seats carries a persona name, and the chain switches the persona setting on in the form title (seat_personas): the name is the title of the seat and changes nothing the seat does. The four Claude seats are called through Anthropic's API (provider anthropic) and need an Anthropic key; the other eleven models are called through OpenRouter and need an OpenRouter key. Every OpenRouter seat asks OpenRouter not to route it to the Open Inference provider (provider.ignore). Every layer has at least two judges. A layer is asked only when every layer below it signed off, and a layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser and the climb starts again at layer 1; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. PENDING: this chain's review limits (7 overseer rounds in maxOverseerRounds, 7 revisions of layer 1 and 3 of layer 2 in layerRevisions) and its rules for sending a plan back are copied from plan-high-council and are not settled. They are being decided in the second debate on the judge system, from the maintainer's rulings of 28 Oct 2026 (layer-1 revisions) and 29 Oct 2026 (the top layer reads every plan before a run ends, a layer that has used its revisions sends the plan up to the next layer with its open objections, and early finish is not wanted), so do not read these numbers as the final design. When the overseer-round limit or layer 1's revision limit is reached the run stops, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose: continue (it extends the limit that was reached; the run's spending limit still applies), or finish (the dispute stage and the handoff run and the result stays "not agreed"), or revise the draft yourself. When layer 2 has used its revisions in an overseer round and objects again, the plan goes up to layer 3 instead of stopping, while a pass is left. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages, and the decider, need a Claude Code session (provider external): they pause the run (exit 3) until the session answers, and the answers should come from a separate fresh session, not the one that wrote the plan. Every API seat reasons at high, except Qwen 3.8 27B: the reasoning table has no effort field for that model, so it runs at its own default, xhigh; no Grok. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6 Luna 128,000; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; MiMo V2.6 Pro and GLM-5.3 Flash 131,072; Qwen 3.8 27B 65,536; Hy4 Preview 64,000; Gemini 4 Argon 32,768. For Kimi K3.1 Pro and MiniMax M3.1 Flash no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Gemini 4 Argon's cap is Google's limit for one non-streaming request, and its thinking tokens count inside it, so a long reply at high effort can be cut off at the cap. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The dry run's expected figure and its upper estimate leave out the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices), so they are not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run. The review judges' proposals and improvement ideas are quoted; the writer's answers are its own claim, and no judge gives a verdict on them.
